newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Dlr/yen vol curve inversion steepens again.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Dlr/yen vol curve inversion steepens again.

text.p: The dollar/yen options volatility curve, which had become virtually flat earlier in the day, steepened its inversion again as the dollar tumbled below 115 yen, dealers said.

Until U.S. morning trade, the curve had been flattening gradually all week as the dollar drifted in the mid-115 to mid-116 yen area, with the relatively plump shorter dates looking increasingly vulnerable as the weekend approached.
"The problem with dollar/yen, and to a certain extent the sterling, is that it (spot) gaps," said a U.S. bank trader in Chicago. "It sits there for a long time and then it gaps."
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility bounced back to about 10.4/10.6 percent at U.S. midsession, about where it ended on Thursday, after dipping about half a point earlier in the day.

In early U.S. trading, after a relatively mild reaction to the May U.S. employment report, volatilities for one-month all the way out to one-year leveled at around 10.0/10.2 percent. One-year has since also risen somewhat to 10.1/10.3 percent.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which gives them quicker accleration against movement in spot rates but is accompanied with higher theta decay.

"If you're short at the wrong time, you're hurting, but it's tough to hold on to a long gamma position when it sits the way it has for the past two weeks," the Chicago trader said of wariness to hold short dates that had grown in the past few days. "That's why you see the one-month pop up so quickly when you have a move like today's," he said.
The dollar's slide toward 114.50 yen today would likely halt the recent decline in volatilities, traders said.
"It's in the direction everyone has been anticipating, but it looks like support is crumbling," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York.
She said the dollar's May lows toward 112 yen now seemed to be a reachable target.
Risk-reversals, the put/call pricing differential, widened their skew for downside yen calls. One-month 25-delta was pegged at 1.2/1.6 point in favor of yen calls.
On the other hand, implied volatilities for dollar/mark options surrendered early gains as the dollar slid toward 1.72 marks after spiking up to a 39-month high of 1.7423 earlier.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility stood at 9.0/9.3 percent, just above Thursday's close, after trading at a high near 9.5 earlier today.

Traders said risk was still perceived to be on the dollar's upside due to rekindled concerns that the introduction of a single European currency could be delayed or that the currency would be unstable.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal was assessed at 0.2/0.5 point bid for mark puts.

There was talk that wipe-out of some large range-binary options that traded Thursday caused turbulence near the dollar's highs today. The upper barrier of the range binaries, which disappear when spot breaks out of predetermined ranges, was said to have been been at 1.7350 marks.
